查看原文（29行） ```text ## The three layers 1. **ENTRY — can it be recognized, installed, and started?** - Checkable compatibility gate. - Use `dsh-standards`; do not infer a pass from the manifest alone. - `recognized` is not the same as `runtime`; `static` is not a pass. 2. **FLOW — can a user install, configure, use, upgrade, and remove it without fighting it?** - J1–J8 user journeys. - Runtime evidence is required for a runtime claim; `not-run` is not a pass. - The flow harness is still a draft; report its limits honestly. 3. **BOOST — does it use Cordis well?** - LEV-1–8 practices: effects, inject/get, volatile config, event modes, seams, stable prompt prefixes, bounded parallel/jobs, composition. - This is a **practice library**, not a grade. It has evidence cards, not a plugin-level pass/fail. - Never turn BOOST into a certification or a score. ## Route the work - **Run a check:** `npx dsh-standards --scope entry --entry-claim static` for recognition; add a host/runtime when claiming runtime. - **Three-layer self-check:** `npx -p dsh-standards dsh-levels --format json`. - **Build or scaffold a plugin:** use the `dsh-primer` skill/CLI. The old `dsh-plugin-dev` command belongs to `dsh-primer`, not to this guide. - **Read the rules:** `dsh-plugin-spec`; **read the guide:** this package; **run the checks:** `dsh-standards`. ```

ENTRY is a compatibility gate, not a full quality audit. It is the first thing a market, index, or user hits. ## What it covers - package manifest: name, version, license, entry, `dsh.bundle.patch` - engines/peer range for the DSH and Cordis generation being claimed - Node `>=24.9.0` for the 0.2.2 line; `engines.dsh`, when declared, decides alone since 0.2.1-alpha.4 (prereleases participate) - the declared entry point actually resolves - the bundle patch parses and its target row resolves - display metadata, labels, and forbidden-claim checks - a runtime claim: plugin start or bundle G0–G3, when evidence is supplied The exact rule IDs and evidence rules are in [`31-DSH-ENTRY`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-standards/blob/main/31-DSH-ENTRY%E5%85%A5%E9%97%A8%E8%A7%84%E8%8C%83.md) and [`40-checker`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-standards/tree/main/40-checker). ## The two claims | Claim | Meaning | What it needs | |---|---|---| | `static` / `recognized` | the package shape can be identified | manifest/entry inspection only | | `runtime` | it actually starts or boots | plugin L1, or bundle G0–G3 | `recognized` is not a pass. A bundle is not proven by importing its server entry; it needs G0–G3. A client-only package is build-only unless a browser probe exists. ## Run it ```sh # Recognition only npx dsh-standards ./my-plugin --scope entry --entry-claim static # Runtime claim: provide the real host/runtime, not a stub npx dsh-standards ./my-bundle --scope entry \ --host /path/to/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js # Machine-readable output npx dsh-standards ./my-plugin --scope entry --entry-claim static --format json ``` Exit codes: `0` completed, `1` attributable FAIL, `2` incomplete/not-run, `3` usage error. A `not-run` or `incomplete` result must not be written as a pass. ## Author checklist - `package.json` has a resolvable entry and, for bundles, a `dsh.bundle.patch`. - The patch target row exists; ordered patch arrays are allowed. - `engines.dsh` or an `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer range is declared. For 0.2.2, prefer `>=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0`; npm default semver needs an explicit `^0.2.2-alpha.3` union arm. - `dsh.capabilities` lists every host surface the plugin touches (see below). - `dsh.labels` is declared when the plugin modifies prompts, runs red-team workloads, adds a model provider, exposes remote access, or mirrors another project. - The license is present; a missing license is advisory, not a fabricated pass. - Module scope stays side-effect free: no top-level `await`, timer, `process.on`, fs write, or subprocess spawn. Do that work in `apply()` and clean up with `ctx.effect()`. - README says how to install and what it needs. - No “official”, “certified”, “secure”, or ranking claim. ## Declaration fields Two optional fields become checks `DSC-11` and `DSC-13` once they exist: ```json { "dsh": { "capabilities": ["fs:read", "network:egress"], "labels": ["remote-access"] } } ``` Allowed `capabilities`: `fs:read`, `fs:write`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `network:egress`, `network:ingress`, `credentials:read`, `credentials:list`, `credentials:provider`, `llm:adapter`, `sessions:read`, `system-prompt:write`, `tools:register`, `remote:expose`, `plugin:install`. Allowed `labels`: `prompt-modification`, `red-team`, `third-party-model-provider`, `remote-access`, `mirror`. Do not label a plugin `official`, `verified`, `certified`, `secure`, or `audited` — those words are treated as an endorsement claim and fail `DSC-13`. ## Import-time side effects `DSC-10` is advisory — it never changes the verdict — but it records module-scope work that runs before `apply()`: top-level `await`, timers, `process.on`, fs writes, and subprocess spawns. There is no `flow-warn` status — a partial run is `not-run`, not a soft pass. `not-run` is never a pass. Do not publish a pass rate or a grade from FLOW. ## Current limit The runtime harness is still a draft. J1/J2/J4/J6 have runtime evidence on fixtures; J3/J7 have fixture-level runtime; J5/J8 have static preflight; browser rendering is not yet covered. The guide must state which journey was actually run. The source harness lives in [`40-checker/scripts/journey.mjs`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-standards/blob/main/40-checker/scripts/journey.mjs) and [`journey-runtime.mjs`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-standards/blob/main/40-checker/scripts/journey-runtime.mjs). The three-layer audit reads FLOW evidence through `--flow-evidence`: ```sh npx -p dsh-standards dsh-levels ./my-plugin --flow-evidence flow.json --format json ``` ## Author checklist - README has Quickstart, Permissions, Config, Upgrade/Uninstall, and Troubleshooting. - Errors say what happened, what to run next, and where the doc is. - Permissions say what the plugin can/cannot do and how to turn it off. - Upgrade and uninstall are tested against real data, not only a clean install. - No “certified”, “verified”, “audited”, “official”, “secure”, or “ranked” wording. It records practices and evidence; it does not attach a “Boost level” to a plugin. The canonical text is [`33-DSH-BOOST`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-standards/blob/main/33-DSH-BOOST%E5%8A%A0%E9%80%9F%E5%AE%9E%E8%B7%B5.md). ## The eight practices | ID | Practice | Evidence to look for | |---|---|---| | LEV-1 | reversible effects | timers, connections, watchers, and subprocesses are in `ctx.effect()` with a label; restart returns to baseline | | LEV-2 | waiting correctly | required services in `inject`; `ctx.inject()` for waits; `ctx.get()` for optional; no polling | | LEV-3 | hot configuration | adjustable fields use `volatile()` + `.get()`; a config change does not restart the plugin | | LEV-4 | event discipline | event name/`@mode` match; waterfall observers call `next()`; serial/bail/parallel for waits; emit for observation | | LEV-5 | seams and isolation | consumers use seams; no implementation imports; isolate/group only when multiple instances need it; per-agent `agent.ctx` | | LEV-6 | stable prefix / assembly | tool and prompt declarations are byte-stable; volatile text goes through `systemPrompt.context`; assembly is reused | | LEV-7 | bounded parallel / long work | independent calls are bounded-parallel; long work uses jobs; cancellation propagates | | LEV-8 | composition / evidence cards | bundle patches and presets express differences; each practice has a reproducible evidence card | ## Evidence, not a badge An evidence card is per practice, per plugin, with a baseline and an after measurement. Example shape: ```yaml practice: LEV-6 plugin: "@acme/dsh-hello@0.1.0" baseline: startupMs: 180 tokensPerTurn: 1200 after: startupMs: 150 tokensPerTurn: 900 environment: dsh: 0.2.2-alpha.3 cordis: 4.0.6-alpha.2 node: 24.9 command: "node bench/hello.mjs" result: "startup 180→150 ms; tokens 1200→900" negativeControl: "same bench with the plugin disabled" generatedAt: "2026-11-03" expiresAt: "2027-05-03" recordHash: "sha256:<64 hex of this record>" claimLevel: "self-assessed" # self-reported | self-assessed | host-reviewed | independent | reference issuer: "author" selfAssessed: true ``` All thirteen fields are required. A missing or malformed field makes the card `not-measured`; a status word alone is not evidence. If an effect cannot be measured (developer hours, maintenance cost, “fewer pitfalls”), record it as a WARN or a note. Do not invent a number. ## Current limits - The measured examples are fixture-level, provider-capture, or synthetic timer results. They are not production baselines. - LEV-3, LEV-6, and LEV-7 have the strongest current evidence; the others have loader/context-level fixtures. - BOOST is not a market gate and must not become a certification. ## Run the audit ```sh npx -p dsh-standards dsh-levels ./my-plugin \ --boost-evidence boost.json --format json ``` Without evidence, the result is `not-measured`, not a pass. See [`40-checker`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-standards/tree/main/40-checker) for the evidence schema and examples. ## Author checklist - Every timer/listener/connection has a disposer owned by the plugin. - Required services are declared; optional services use `ctx.get()`. - User-tunable fields are volatile, not hard-coded. - Waterfall listeners either call `next()` or deliberately short-circuit. - Tool/prompt prefixes are stable; volatile text is outside the prefix. - Long work is cancellable and does not block a turn. - Each claimed improvement has a command, environment, and raw artifact.
